name: ConfirmationDialog
statusNote: A thin, fixed configuration of Dialog that has shipped for years; alpha because it inherits Dialog's status. It allows no custom header, body renderer or footer.
summary: A Dialog that asks one question and offers exactly two buttons, cancel and confirm, and reports which closed it. Use it to confirm an action, especially a destructive one; use dialog when the task needs a form or more than two choices.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: The question, usually short. It is the dialog's heading and accessible name.

inputs.name: confirmButtonContent
inputs.description: Label of the confirm button. Prefer a verb that names the action.

inputs.name: confirmButtonType
inputs.description: Variant of the confirm button; normal is Button's default variant. danger also moves initial focus to cancel.

inputs.name: cancelButtonLoading
inputs.description: Show the cancel button in its loading state.

inputs.name: confirmButtonLoading
inputs.description: Show the confirm button in its loading state, e.g. while the confirmed action runs.

inputs.name: overrideButtonFocus
inputs.description: Force which button takes initial focus. Rarely right: it can make a dangerous action one keypress away.

inputs.name: onClose
inputs.description: Called with confirm, cancel, close-button or escape (a backdrop click reports escape). The caller closes the dialog.

anatomy.name: Dialog
anatomy.description: A Dialog with role alertdialog: backdrop, window, title bar with close button, body. See dialog for all geometry, motion and tokens.

anatomy.name: Cancel button
anatomy.description: The first footer button, Button default variant, labelled cancelButtonContent.

anatomy.name: Confirm button
anatomy.description: The second (trailing) footer button, in confirmButtonType's variant, labelled confirmButtonContent.

variants.description: Confirm is a default Button; it takes initial focus.
Confirm is a primary Button; it takes initial focus.
Confirm is a danger Button; cancel takes initial focus so Enter does not destroy.

layout.text: Width defaults to medium (320px); everything else (backdrop, centring, header, 16px body, right-aligned footer with 8px gaps) is Dialog's.
The footer always holds cancel then confirm, in that order, so confirm sits at the trailing end.

states.text: cancelButtonLoading and confirmButtonLoading put that button in Button's loading state (spinner, ignores activation, keeps focus); the dialog stays open and the other button stays live.
Enters as Dialog does: 200ms backdrop fade and a 200ms scale-fade of the window from 0.5.

behaviour.text: Initial focus goes to confirm, unless confirmButtonType is danger, in which case it goes to cancel; overrideButtonFocus replaces that choice.
Cancel calls onClose('cancel'); confirm calls onClose('confirm'); the header X calls onClose('close-button'); Escape and a backdrop click call onClose('escape'). The dialog never closes itself.
useConfirm offers an awaitable form: it mounts a ConfirmationDialog in a fresh root, resolves true when the gesture was confirm and false for any other, and unmounts on close.
Focus trap, focus return to the element focused before opening, Escape handling, scroll lock and footer arrow-key navigation all come from Dialog.

keyboard: Enter or Space activates the focused button; with a danger confirm that is Cancel by default.
ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move between Cancel and the confirm button.
semantics: role alertdialog, labelled by the title.
Content is in the body; it is not wired as the description (there is no subtitle), so assistive technology reads it as the dialog's content, not its description.

notes.text: A backdrop click reports escape, so callers that treat anything but confirm as cancel get the right result, but a caller cannot tell a backdrop click from the Escape key.

useConfirm creates a new React root on the document body for each call and resolves a promise. A native build exposes the same outcome as a modal call or a pending result the frame loop polls: true only for confirm.

There is no subtitle, so the dialog's aria-describedby points at an element that does not exist (Dialog's dangling description id). A native build should describe the alertdialog by its body text instead, which is what an alert dialog needs.

Initial focus relies on Dialog's autoFocus footer button; Dialog also re-focuses that button on its second render to recover when the dialog opened from inside another focus trap. A native build sets focus once after the dialog's trap is active.
